purpose: Known resistance cases and the drug classes a profile must (and must not) report as defeated. Issue #17. Expected sets are minimal on purpose: a CARD update that adds a class must not break them, but a profile that loses one or gains a forbidden one must.
review_note: The expectations are the author's reading of standard microbiology checked against CARD's web pages. No domain expert has reviewed them yet. Have one do so before they are used as evidence in the writeup.
slice: card_slice/4.0.2 (regenerate with the command in docs/profiling-known-cases.md)

cases.basis: Each gene's classes and mechanisms were compared with its page at card.mcmaster.ca on 2026-11-07 (docs/card-spot-check.md): they match, except mecA, whose page also lists carbapenem and monobactam. Absent classes: ESBLs such as CTX-M-15 do not hydrolyse carbapenems and carry no quinolone, aminoglycoside or tetracycline activity. CARD also lists azole and imidazole for CTX-M-15; that is surprising, is deliberately not asserted either way, and should be queried with CARD.

cases.description: MRSA: mecA alone, in Staphylococcus aureus.
cases.basis: Each gene's classes and mechanisms were compared with its page at card.mcmaster.ca on 2026-11-07 (docs/card-spot-check.md): they match, except mecA, whose page also lists carbapenem and monobactam. Absent: no link on the gene's CARD page, and not part of the gene's known resistance phenotype. Carbapenem (and, for mecC, cephalosporin) is not in CARD's August 2026 download but is on CARD's website and in the curated supplement, which cites Gajdacs 2019, Antibiotics 8(2):52, PMID 31052511 (abstract: MRSA with an altered PBP2a/c is resistant to all penicillins, cephalosporins and carbapenems).

cases.description: MRSA carrying mecC, the divergent PBP2a homologue, in Staphylococcus aureus.
cases.basis: CARD's download links mecC only to penicillin beta-lactam, while its website lists penicillin, cephalosporin and carbapenem (docs/card-spot-check.md). Cephalosporin and carbapenem come from the curated supplement, citing Gajdacs 2019 (PMID 31052511). Absent: no link on the gene's CARD page, and not part of the gene's known resistance phenotype.

cases.description: MRSA that is also fluoroquinolone resistant: mecA plus the S84L change in S. aureus gyrA.
cases.basis: Each gene's classes and mechanisms were compared with its page at card.mcmaster.ca on 2026-11-07 (docs/card-spot-check.md): they match, except mecA, whose page also lists carbapenem and monobactam. S84L is among the gyrA changes CARD lists for the S. aureus model. Absent: no link on the gene's CARD page, and not part of the gene's known resistance phenotype. Carbapenem (and, for mecC, cephalosporin) is not in CARD's August 2026 download but is on CARD's website and in the curated supplement, which cites Gajdacs 2019, Antibiotics 8(2):52, PMID 31052511 (abstract: MRSA with an altered PBP2a/c is resistant to all penicillins, cephalosporins and carbapenems).

cases.description: The shipped typical resistant S. aureus (mecA, tet(K), msrA, blaZ).
cases.basis: Each gene's classes and mechanisms were compared with its page at card.mcmaster.ca on 2026-11-07 (docs/card-spot-check.md): they match, except mecA, whose page also lists carbapenem and monobactam. tet(K) is a tetracycline efflux pump; msrA protects the ribosome against macrolides and streptogramin B. Absent: no link on the gene's CARD page, and not part of the gene's known resistance phenotype. Carbapenem (and, for mecC, cephalosporin) is not in CARD's August 2026 download but is on CARD's website and in the curated supplement, which cites Gajdacs 2019, Antibiotics 8(2):52, PMID 31052511 (abstract: MRSA with an altered PBP2a/c is resistant to all penicillins, cephalosporins and carbapenems).

cases.description: The shipped typical resistant K. pneumoniae (KPC-2, CTX-M-15, SHV-1, OXA-1, oqxA, oqxB, FosA).
cases.basis: Each gene's classes and mechanisms were compared with its page at card.mcmaster.ca on 2026-11-07 (docs/card-spot-check.md): they match, except mecA, whose page also lists carbapenem and monobactam. KPC-2 is a carbapenemase; oqxA and oqxB form an efflux pump that reduces fluoroquinolone susceptibility; FosA inactivates fosfomycin. Absent: no link on the gene's CARD page, and not part of the gene's known resistance phenotype.

cases.description: The shipped typical resistant A. baumannii (OXA-23, OXA-51, ADC-25, adeB, adeJ).
cases.basis: Each gene's classes and mechanisms were compared with its page at card.mcmaster.ca on 2026-11-07 (docs/card-spot-check.md): they match, except mecA, whose page also lists carbapenem and monobactam. OXA-23 is an acquired carbapenem-hydrolysing oxacillinase; ADC-25 is the chromosomal cephalosporinase; AdeABC/AdeIJK efflux affects fluoroquinolones and tetracyclines. Aminoglycoside is deliberately not forbidden: AdeABC is known to contribute to aminoglycoside resistance even though CARD's adeB page does not list it. Absent: no link on the gene's CARD page, and not part of the gene's known resistance phenotype.
